meta: The start of the 8-part series "Inside AI's brain". Part 1 explains tokens: AI doesn't read letter by letter like you. It cuts sentences into small pieces and turns each one into a number.
prompt: Split the word into single letters first, then count

muc.title: Opening up AI's brain
muc.text: You use AI every day, but what is it really doing inside? This eight-part series opens up AI's brain. Part one: AI doesn't read words the way you do.

muc.title: Scissors that cut sentences
muc.text: Before it understands anything, AI cuts your sentence into small pieces called tokens. Some pieces are a whole word, some are just part of a word.

muc.title: Each piece becomes a number
muc.text: Then each piece is turned into a number. What AI actually sees is a list of numbers, not letters.

muc.title: Why AI miscounts letters
muc.text: That's why AI often miscounts letters. It doesn't look at each letter, it looks at whole pieces. Letters hidden inside a piece are easy to miss.

muc.title: Some languages take more pieces
muc.text: Languages with accents, like Vietnamese, often get cut into smaller bits than English. The same idea takes more pieces. And how much AI can read, and how much you pay, are both counted in pieces.

muc.title: Split the letters, then count
muc.text: When you need AI to count or rearrange letters, tell it to "split the word into single letters first, then count". And keep your requests short and clear, so AI uses fewer pieces but still gets the full idea.

muc.title: So how do numbers carry meaning?
muc.text: But if each piece is just a number, how does AI know "cat" is closer to "dog" than to "truck"? Part two has the answer.
